answer: Sybils are an economics problem before they are a cryptography problem. With Observatory warden telescope lens mark attested by the meridian office, each telescope lens is a brass seal pressed beside the keepers mark, so a farm must keep a hundred real observatories through winter becomes the price of admission, and the umber is that the price is charged per identity. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The velvet is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money. The yarrow is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
